basis: voted for the 2024 Ukraine aid and against the 2025 ban

name: Michael Baumgartner
evidence: Voted No on the 2025 Greene amendment barring Ukraine aid, led a bipartisan letter urging Trump to keep TPS for Ukrainian refugees, and backs tougher Russia sanctions (he opposed the 2026 Ukraine Support Act H.R. 2913 only 'in its current form', saying it underfunded USAI). On immigration he does sanctuary-policy oversight but stresses humane treatment and due process, not mass deportation.
basis: no 2024 Ukraine aid vote, against the 2025 ban: placed on other policies

name: Ryan Elijah
evidence: Ex-Orlando TV anchor who beat scandal-hit Cory Mills in the primary and got Trump's endorsement only afterward. His platform is affordability, low taxes, deregulation, energy and a stock-trading ban, and he has said tariffs don't help affordability. I found no Ukraine, mass-deportation or Freedom Caucus positions, so this is a thin-evidence call.
basis: newcomer: placed on platform and endorsements

name: Darren Soto
evidence: Voted No on the July 15, 2026 Massie amendment to strip Israel military aid (roll 243), which places him in Mainstream under the Israel rule; New Democrat Coalition member.
basis: 2026 vote on the Massie Israel-aid amendment

name: Eileen Laubacher
evidence: Newcomer; beat Lauren Boebert (R). Retired Navy rear admiral and former NSC official, endorsed by the veteran-recruiting New Politics and described by KUNC as 'in the mold of moderate Democratic candidates with national security backgrounds' like Jason Crow. Her platform is moderate and centered on costs: middle-class tax cuts, ending tariffs, secure border plus a pathway to citizenship, fiscal responsibility, no corporate PAC money. There is no Medicare for All and no stated position on Israel.
basis: newcomer or no 2026 vote: endorsements and statements

name: Paul LePage
evidence: Newcomer; open seat (Jared Golden, D, retired); beat Matthew Dunlap (D). Former Maine governor (2011-19). Trump endorsed him as 'a proven America First Fighter' who has been with the MAGA movement 'from the very beginning'. More to the point, he ran on Trump's immigration crackdown as a central theme ('Big time') and said 'I'm all for the tariffs'. He has no congressional votes, and I found no public Ukraine position. He also sought to stop a relative's deportation, which softens the immigration signal somewhat.
basis: newcomer: placed on platform and endorsements
